name: Marie Curie
role: Scientist, Discoverer & Quiet Fighter of the Dark
famous_quote: Nothing in life is to be feared, it is only to be understood.
story_childhood:
In a busy city called Warsaw,
a baby girl was born.

Her name was Maria.
Everyone called her Manya.

She loved to read.
She read everything she found.

Her father taught science.
He kept shiny tools on a shelf.

Manya stared at them for hours.
She wanted to know how things worked.
story_takeaway: Keep working, one small step at a time, and the dark will give up its secrets.

modern.title: If Marie Were 10 Today
modern.narrative:
If Marie were ten today,
she would love the library.

She would ask endless questions
in her science class.

She might code little robots.
She might study glowing stars.

When something seemed too hard,
she would try once more.

She would tell shy girls
that their ideas matter too.

The world would be her lab.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Loved to Learn
chapters.narrative:
Manya was very clever.
She won prizes at school.

But girls could not go
to university back then.

That did not stop her.
She studied in secret classes.

She saved every coin.
She dreamed of far-off Paris.

She worked as a teacher
to help her sister first.

Her turn would come.
She was sure of it.

chapters.title: Paris and Pale Blue Light
chapters.narrative:
At last she reached Paris.
She changed her name to Marie.

She was often cold and hungry.
She ate only bread and tea.

But she loved her studies.
Numbers and metals filled her days.

She met a kind man, Pierre.
He loved science too.

Together they wondered
about strange, glowing rocks.

What made them shine?

chapters.title: The Cold, Leaky Shed
chapters.narrative:
They worked in an old shed.
Rain dripped through the roof.

Marie stirred huge boiling pots.
Her arms ached every night.

She boiled tons of rock
to find a tiny speck.

Many said she would fail.
Marie did not listen.

For four long years
she stirred and waited.

At last, in the dark,
something glowed.

timeline.caption: Maria is born in Warsaw, Poland.
She moves to Paris to study science.
Marie and Pierre discover radium and polonium.
She wins her first Nobel Prize in Physics.
She wins a second Nobel Prize, in Chemistry.

after_treasures.title: Gifts That Live On
after_treasures.narrative:
Marie gave the world
more than shining metals.

She gave us new ideas.
She gave us courage.

Her work helps doctors
find and fight disease.

Her name still means
never, ever give up.

Each gift below
came from her patient hands.

All from a girl
who loved to learn.

lessons.lesson: Keep going even when the work is slow and hard.
Ask how things work, then go and find out.
Do brave things even when others doubt you.
Share what you learn to help other people.
